analysis:
Examined all 12 supplied batch analyses and every replayed source unit. Replay is incomplete (6 of 65 reviewed units; 59 omitted), so the reported candidate findings cannot be independently validated from their cited caller/source-gate lines. They remain material review questions, not cleared concerns.

Visible changes move dev publication from master to dev pushes and introduce Developer ID signing/notarization. release-provider.yml:142–145 supplies the lane environment to verify-source; :829–834 strengthens final archived-app verification with Apple anchor, provider identifier and team requirements. docs/developer/test.md:1048–1059 documents the same-branch reusable caller, secrets inheritance and shared Apple credentials; :1066–1078 describes dev-only resolution and verified dev ancestry. These establish an expanded release trust contract, but neither secret inheritance nor shared signing identity alone proves unauthorized access or production qualification. The replayed identity-test change is comment-only; changelogs and test documentation do not prove execution or deployment controls.

Further review must recover release-dev-branch.yml BASE/HEAD, particularly HEAD:95–106, and provider_release_resume/api.py:73–94. Independently determine whether branch-controlled workflow logic can bypass master-owned verification or access shared/prod credentials, and reconcile the runbook's reported review prerequisite with actual activation controls. Check resolver environment confinement, trusted script revisions in credentialed jobs, artifact/source binding, publication serialization and updater lane selection. Relevant contracts are A-005/A-011/A-017, T-013/T-034/T-054 and TB-011: signing/publication must remain distinct from independently approved serving authorization (T-052/T-056). Resolve these questions before accepting or dismissing the two local candidates.

No replayed executable change directly alters hop encryption, plaintext handling, tenant cache isolation (T-041), billing, inference admission or fan-helper authority. This limited evidence does not establish a concrete regression in those controls or constitute release clearance.
